result.dimension: In-window travel guard protection over a long window at linear 300

findings.title: step_path_contained sizes the corridor from max_travel_m only — no wall-clock bound, so a no-op guard is uncontained
findings.summary: `required = max_travel_m + stop_overshoot_m` (4.5 + 0.50 = 5.00 m) assumes the distance guard works. The same repo already corrected exactly this reasoning in the other probe: `corridor_must_cover_m` at services.py:7933-7944 is `max(max_travel_m + overshoot, _PROBE_SPEED_PER_LINEAR_UNIT_MS * linear_speed * duration_ms)` with the comment "WORST CASE, not the nominal one — corrected 2026-08-23 … This previously reported max_travel_m + overshoot, which assumes the guard works." The step probe never got that fix, and its window length is what the cap-raise proposal moves.
findings.failure_scenario: A documented guard no-op mode exists and is pinned by this repo's own test (tests/components/mammotion/test_step_response_probe.py:487, "payloads arrived carrying stale coordinates … while a FROZEN one means no position payloads arrived at all"): position payloads keep arriving with advancing `sequence` and fresh `received_at_monotonic` but latched x/y — the 2026-08-28 event (21 bit-identical samples while the mower travelled 0.4375 m) and the attempt-3 blind travel (0.5097 m observed as 0.021 m). In that mode `_apply_travel_guard` trips on nothing: `dropped_samples` unchanged, `sequence == prev+1`, `epoch` unchanged, `age_ms` fresh, `valid_for_motion` true, and `cumulative_distance_m` stays ~0. The window then runs to the wall clock. Concretely: linear 400, baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 = 23000 ms (the current cap), max_travel_m 4.5, corridor validated at clearance >= 5.00 m. At the measured full-window rate of the 2026-09-01 run (0.2655 m/s) the mower covers 6.11 m — 6.44 m on the sizing constant `_PROBE_SPEED_PER_LINEAR_UNIT_MS` — plus the 0.4544 m measured post-stop creep, i.e. ~6.6 m inside a corridor proven to hold 5.00 m: a ~1.6 m breach of an open-loop curved path. Under the proposed 30000 ms cap the same scenario gives ~8.4 m against the unchanged 5.00 m requirement, a ~3.4 m breach. `travel_projection` (services.py:10135) does not cover this — it compares floor/typical travel against `max_travel_m`, is explicitly non-blocking, and says nothing about the corridor radius a no-op guard needs.

findings.title: Travel-guard sequence baseline is read from handle.latest_position_sample after the movement command is sent, racing the queue
findings.summary: `guard_state["sequence"]` is seeded from `handle.latest_position_sample.sequence` at sampler-task start, but the queue was last drained by `_wait_for_position_subscription_ready` (services.py:10274) — before `_send_manager_command_with_args` and `asyncio.create_task`. pymammotion sets `_latest_position_sample` and offers the sample to the stream in the same statement block (device/handle.py:692-694), so any payload published in that gap advances the baseline AND sits in the queue. The guard then demands `sequence == baseline + 1` (services.py:7640) and trips on the sample it should have accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: Readiness returns with origin sequence N (queue now empty, `latest.sequence == N`). The `send_movement` dispatch takes 73-259 ms on the five banked runs (up to ~1.3 s of BLE write latency is on record in this project). A position payload publishes during that gap: the queue holds sequence N+1 and `latest.sequence` becomes N+1. `_capture_in_window_telemetry` seeds `guard_state["sequence"] = N+1`. On the first 100 ms tick it drains N+1, compares against the expected N+2, and returns `_trip("position_sequence_gap")` — `travel_abort` set, refresh loop stopped, mandatory stop sent at ~100 ms with `cumulative_travel_m: 0.0`. At the ~1 Hz publication rate that is roughly a 7-26% chance per run at the measured dispatch latencies, and higher on a degraded link. It is fail-closed, but it silently burns a supervised, separately-authorized real-mower run and reproduces the exact signature (`position_sequence_gap`, `travel_at_trip_m: 0.0`) that was previously misattributed to `maxsize=1` on 2026-08-30. No test covers a sample arriving between readiness and sampler start.

findings.title: Stale-feed clock is reset to now at sampler start instead of the origin sample's receipt time
findings.summary: `guard_state["last_receipt_at"] = time.monotonic()` discards the origin sample's `received_at_monotonic`, so the 2000 ms `_PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS` budget restarts from the sampler's start rather than from the last real position payload. This is the fail-open direction on the only detector that catches a dead inbound feed.
findings.failure_scenario: The origin position payload is consumed by the readiness wait at T. The `send_movement` dispatch plus task scheduling costs ~0.2 s, so the sampler starts at T+0.2 and seeds `last_receipt_at = T+0.2`. If the feed then dies outright, the `position_sample is None` branch (services.py:7634-7638) does not trip until T+2.2 s — and since the last genuine payload could itself have been up to ~1.1 s old at T (max measured motion inter-arrival gap 1316.5 ms across 70 banked intervals), the mower drives up to ~3.3 s of real feed silence before the abort, ~0.88 m at 0.2655 m/s, instead of the 2.0 s / ~0.53 m the constant states. Seeding from `origin_sample.received_at_monotonic` closes it.

findings.title: RTK course_series informativeness floor (0.15 m chord) is censored at linear 300
findings.summary: `_step_response_course_series` is called with `min_chord_m=config.min_travel_for_heading_trust_m` = 0.15 m (continuous_controller.py:121). At linear 300 the position feed still arrives at ~1 Hz, so the chord is set by speed alone: 0.16 m/s gives ~0.16-0.18 m chords, only 7-20% above the floor, and the pre-dispatch floor speed of 0.10 m/s (`_STEP_RESPONSE_MIN_SPEED_BY_LINEAR[300]`) gives ~0.10-0.11 m chords, entirely below it. Nothing in `_apply_travel_guard` needs a minimum displacement, and VIO scoring (2a/2b) is unaffected, so this is diagnostic loss, not a safety defect.
findings.failure_scenario: Phase A of the proposal runs at linear 300 to measure sustained speed for the first time. If the true sustained speed is anywhere near the pessimistic 0.10 m/s floor rather than the extrapolated 0.16 m/s, every entry in `course_series` comes back `informative: false` with `course_degrees: null`, `_step_response_analysis` returns null for both criteria, and the run yields no RTK course track at all — the exact instrument that would cross-check the VIO channel. The single 1316.5 ms inter-arrival gap already in the banked data would push even a 0.16 m/s run's chord to 0.21 m, but a 0.71 s gap (also observed) drops it to 0.11 m, so individual intervals drop out even at the optimistic speed. `chord_m` and `cumulative_travel_m` are still emitted unconditionally, so the speed measurement itself survives.

result.notes:
Answers to the three sub-questions, measured from docs/raw-samples/ (5 runs, 549 samples, 70 consecutive-position chords).

(a) PHANTOM TRAVEL — not a false-trip risk, and it consumes almost nothing. The "2-4 cm noise floor" is the pulsed-measurement artifact; during continuous motion the per-axis position noise estimated by third-differencing the distinct-position track is sigma ~= 0.008 m. The guard sums |chord| between consecutive accepted samples, and the positive bias of that sum is ~sigma_diff^2/(2*d) per interval. At 0.22 m chords (linear 400) that is 6.7 mm over 23 intervals; at 0.16 m chords (linear 300) 9.3 mm over 23 intervals and 12.1 mm over the 30 a proposed 30 s window would give — 0.15-0.27% of the 4.5 m budget. Corroborating: the observed chords are extremely regular (run 1: 0.2233-0.2333 m across 13 intervals). Phantom travel cannot cause a false trip and is not worth budgeting for.

(b) STALE-FEED ABORT over a longer window — the bound still holds on the evidence, with less margin than it looks. Across 70 in-motion position inter-arrival gaps, max 1316.5 ms, typical 0.81-1.12 s, so the worst observed gap sits at 1.52x under the 2000 ms `_PROBE_FEED_STALE_ABORT_MS`. But n=70 comes from 13-15 intervals per run; a 23 s window has ~23 and a 30 s window ~30, so per-run exposure to the tail grows ~60-100%. The beta77 stationary corpus recorded 28 of 1434 intervals (1.95%) above 2.0 s; if the in-motion tail is anywhere comparable, a 30-interval window has a materially non-trivial chance of a false `feed_stale` trip. That is fail-closed (wasted run, not danger) — but combined with finding 3 the effective budget at window start is looser than 2000 ms, which is the direction that matters for safety. Recommend re-deriving the constant against motion intervals, not the stationary corpus, before the cap moves.

(c) MINIMUM PER-SAMPLE DISPLACEMENT — the guard itself requires none (`_apply_travel_guard` has no chord floor; it accepts sequence, epoch, age and `valid_for_motion` only), so a slower speed does not break containment. The only displacement floor in the path is the RTK `course_series` 0.15 m informativeness floor — see the low finding above. VIO scoring (`_step_response_vio_intervals`) keys on distinct heading readings, not displacement, so 2a/2b are speed-independent.

result.dimension: E-VIO scoring correctness at ~15-22 step intervals instead of 7

findings.title: E-VIO half-phase rate aliases at 180 deg of accumulated heading; the current 15 s cap sits 2-5% under it
findings.summary: Each half rate is an ENDPOINT difference pushed through normalize_degrees (wraps to [-180,180)), so a half that accumulates >=180 deg of rotation silently aliases and the half rate flips sign. That was unreachable at 7 s and is marginal at the shipped 15 s cap.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured from docs/raw-samples/raw-route1-run2*-plus180-step7000: the step's second-half VIO mean rate is -11.359 and -11.784 deg/s. The half boundary is chosen by READING COUNT (boundary = len(readings)//2, line 9949), not by time, so a single VIO gap in one half lets the other span nearly the whole step. At the shipped step_ms ceiling of 15000, a half spanning the full step accumulates -170 to -177 deg -- 2-5% from the alias. A run 6% faster than banked (or the proposed 22000 ms step, where even a symmetric half spans 11 s and an asymmetric one spans ~18 s) crosses it: an actual -181 deg is read as +179, the half rate flips from ~-11.9 to ~+11.9 deg/s, and half_diff jumps to ~24 deg/s -> spurious 2a FAIL on a perfectly steady step. Worse in the other direction: if BOTH halves wrap, the diff can land back under 1.5 deg/s -> spurious 2a PASS, and omega_step_deg_per_s is then published with the WRONG SIGN (line 10032, half_rates[1]) and divides rotation_after_zero to produce a nonsense tau_actuator_s -- exactly the ramp-sampled-omega class of error 2a exists to prevent, but with no guard because the number looks steady. Fix: accumulate the already-normalized per-interval deltas across the half (each ~1 Hz interval is far below 180 deg) instead of differencing the two endpoints.

findings.title: vio_analysis scores a travel-guard-aborted window against nominal phase boundaries, with no truncation marker
findings.summary: _step_response_vio_analysis is handed the nominal baseline_ms/step_ms and never sees motion_refresh['aborted_early'], so a run cut short by the travel guard is scored as if every phase ran to plan and returns scoreable: true with published omega/tau.
findings.failure_scenario: The file's own comment at line 9556 states a 23 s window at linear 400 projects 4.97 m against the unchanged max_travel_m of 4.5, while the pre-dispatch blocker uses the 0.17 LOWER bound (0.17*23 = 3.91 m) and lets it through -- so at the new clock caps a guard trip is EXPECTED, not exceptional (the 15.2 s run of 2026-09-01 already used 89% of budget). Case A, trip during settle (e.g. 3000/15000/5000, guard fires at ~21 s): settle is truncated to ~3 s, which still yields the >=3 intervals 2b requires, so 2b is scored on a settle cut short by a commanded stop and rotation_after_zero (line 10035) integrates only part of the carryover -- tau_actuator_s is published as a measurement from a censored settle, scoreable: true, and nothing inside vio_analysis says the window was truncated (the only signal, result['reason'], lives in a different part of the response). Case B, trip during the step: _hold_until returns False so the scheduler never records the 'settle' transition (line 9730) and the step angular stands until the mandatory stop, meaning the final intervals still labelled 'step' are the stop's deceleration. Those land in 2a's second half and drag its mean down toward the onset-slowed first half, which can turn a still-ramping step into a spurious 2a PASS plus a published omega_step_deg_per_s. Gate on aborted_early (refuse with an unscoreable_reason), or clip the phase boundaries to the last observed phase transition.

findings.title: RTK diagnostic omega_step wraps over the whole step span; guaranteed to alias at the proposed 22 s
findings.summary: _step_response_analysis._rate takes normalize_degrees of first-row-to-last-row course across the ENTIRE step phase, so it aliases once total step rotation reaches 180 deg. The comment above it asserts normalize is correct, which only holds below 180 deg.
findings.failure_scenario: Recomputed from the banked raw samples with the shipped 0.15 m chord floor, the RTK step-phase rotation rate is -10.65 and -10.48 deg/s on the two +180 runs. Extrapolated to the shipped step_ms ceiling of 15000 that is -160 and -157 deg over the step span -- 87-89% of the way to the alias, so a run 13% faster wraps today; at the proposed 22000 it is -234 and -231 deg, which wraps unconditionally. When it does, analysis.omega_step_deg_per_s flips sign (e.g. -234 reads as +126, giving +5.7 deg/s where the truth is -10.6) and analysis.tau_actuator_s, computed as |rotation_after_zero / omega_step| at line 9844, becomes an arbitrary number with no failed criterion attached -- the RTK block has no 2a gate. These fields are still emitted in every response and this project's history shows them being quoted (the discarded tau = 7.28 s). Same fix: sum the per-interval normalized deltas rather than differencing the span endpoints.

result.notes: Checked and found CORRECT, so not reported: (1) the half split -- with k step intervals there are k+1 readings, boundary = (k+1)//2, giving first/second halves of (k+1)//2 and k-(k+1)//2 intervals, i.e. asymmetric by at most one interval with the extra always in the first half (k=7 -> 4/3, k=15 -> 8/7, k=20 -> 10/10); the relative asymmetry SHRINKS with n, and the boundary reading is correctly shared by both halves. (2) The >=3 informative-interval gate is applied to 2a inside _step_response_half_phase_agreement and to 2b at line 10024; both fail closed. (3) tau/omega gating: omega_step exists only when 2a passed (line 10032) and tau only when omega is truthy and both step and settle intervals exist -- correct, and it is what returned nulls on the 2026-09-01 failing run. (4) VIO cadence in the banked data is tight (min interval 711 ms, median ~1015 ms), so there are no pathological short-dt intervals inflating 2b's last-two rates. (5) Phase-by-midpoint straddle at the step/settle boundary is real but small and shrinking with n: the last step-labelled interval extends 0-14% past the nominal boundary in the five banked runs. It does bias rotation_after_zero low by up to ~one VIO period of post-zero rotation (~12 deg at +180), which understates tau -- pre-existing, unchanged by larger n, not reported. (6) The 2b carryover prepend at line 10013 is inert by construction: the pass gate requires >=3 settle intervals, so settle_rates always has >=4 entries and the prepended step interval can never be one of the last two. It is cosmetic rather than wrong, but the field name rates_deg_per_s_including_carryover_from_step advertises an influence the verdict never has.

result.dimension: collateral damage to other callers and previously-valid configs

findings.title: step_window_travel_exceeds_budget refuses every attempt to run with a SMALLER travel guard, making max_travel_m's schema minimum unreachable and rewarding raising the exposure bound
findings.summary: The new pre-dispatch refusal fires whenever `floor_speed x window > max_travel_m`, so it does not only refuse long windows — it refuses SHORT ones whose guard was deliberately set low. Every previously-valid (phases x max_travel_m) pair below that line changed verdict from permitted to refused, and the only two ways out are to shorten the window or to RAISE max_travel_m, which raises both the real exposure and the clearance `step_path_contained` demands.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured by running `_step_response_probe(dry_run=True)` across the matrix on the current tree. At linear 400 the schema defaults (baseline 3000 / step 3000 / settle 4000 = 10 s) are refused for every `max_travel_m` below 1.70 m: 0.10 / 0.30 / 0.50 / 1.00 / 1.50 all return `step_window_travel_exceeds_budget`, where the pre-change tree dispatched all five. The banked route-1 run-1 config (3000/5000/5000 = 13 s) is refused at max_travel_m 1.00 and below; 3000/7000/5000 (15 s, the config of both the 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-01 hardware runs) is refused at 2.50 — the schema's own DEFAULT max_travel_m. Worse, the minimum admissible window is 1000+1000+1000 = 3 s, so `floor_travel_m` is never below 0.51 m at linear 400 (0.30 m at 300): `max_travel_m` values in [0.10, 0.51) at linear 400 and [0.10, 0.30) at linear 300 are now unreachable at EVERY phase combination, although `vol.Range(min=0.10, ...)` (services.py:1022) still advertises them. Concretely: an operator with only ~2.2 m of verified corridor clearance can pass `step_path_contained` only at max_travel_m <= 1.70; at the default 10 s window that is exactly the boundary and anything more conservative (1.50) is refused outright, so the documented recovery is to type a LARGER number. Neither `max_travel_m`'s strings.json description ("Distance guard. Reaching it aborts the window and brings the mandatory stop forward.") nor its services.yaml text mentions that lowering it can refuse the run — the refusal is documented only under `step_ms` — so the blocker reads as unrelated to the field the operator just changed.

findings.title: Raising _STEP_RESPONSE_MAX_TOTAL_MS to 23000 moved the wall-clock travel bound from inside the proven containment disk to outside it, for the maximum-exposure config
findings.summary: `step_path_contained` proves a disk of `max_travel_m + 0.50` m. At the old 16000 ms cap the window clock could not produce more travel than that disk even at the fastest speed the mower has shown; at 23000 ms it can, and the 0.24 -> 0.17 correction to the min-speed table is what re-permitted the pairing (0.24 x 23 = 5.52 > 4.5 refused it; 0.17 x 23 = 3.91 does not).
findings.failure_scenario: linear_speed 400, baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 (23000 ms), max_travel_m 4.5 — confirmed permitted on the current tree (`step_window_travel_exceeds_budget` absent; only the non-blocking `likely_guard_trip: true` flags it). `step_path_contained` requires and proves 4.5 + 0.50 = 5.00 m of clearance in every direction. At the fastest banked linear-400 full-window rate quoted in the table's own comment (0.2616 m/s) a full 23 s window covers 6.02 m — 1.02 m beyond the corridor the gate proved, on an open-loop curved path whose shape is the unknown under test. Under the pre-change 16000 ms cap the same arithmetic gave 4.19 m, comfortably inside the 5.00 m disk, so the clock was an independent bound below containment; it no longer is. This only bites if the cumulative-distance guard under-counts (it sums per-sample chords and cannot see the documented observer-lag case where payloads arrive on schedule — sequence +1, fresh receipt — carrying coordinates lagged behind reality, CLAUDE.md's unresolved possibility (a) from 2026-08-28), but that is exactly the failure the containment disk exists as the last line for, and it has lost its redundant partner. Note the argument is unaffected by the corridor being re-centred each run: the disk radius is fixed at max_travel_m + 0.50 by construction.

findings.title: The two speed tables' .get() fallbacks disagree in direction and now fail OPEN, and travel_projection records a floor_travel_m it cannot attribute to any floor_speed_m_s
findings.summary: `_STEP_RESPONSE_MIN_SPEED_BY_LINEAR.get(int(linear_speed), 0.10)` hands an unlisted speed the SLOWEST floor in the table (so the refusal cannot fire), while `_STEP_RESPONSE_TYPICAL_SPEED_BY_LINEAR.get(int(linear_speed), 0.216)` hands it the FASTEST projection, and the `floor_speed_m_s` field at line 10137 uses no default at all — so the emitted evidence carries a computed `floor_travel_m` with `floor_speed_m_s: null` beside it. Nothing ties the schema's `vol.In([300, 400])` (services.py:987) to the tables' keys.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change adds a measured speed to the schema — e.g. `vol.In([300, 400, 500])` — and forgets one or both tables. A caller then requests linear_speed 500 with baseline 3000 / step 15000 / settle 5000 and max_travel_m 4.5: `floor_travel_m = 0.10 x 23 = 2.30 <= 4.5`, so `step_window_travel_exceeds_budget` never fires for the FASTEST speed in the service, silently granting the loosest bound to the configuration that needs the tightest. `travel_projection` then publishes `{"floor_speed_m_s": null, "floor_travel_m": 2.30, "typical_speed_m_s": null, "typical_travel_m": 4.968, "likely_guard_trip": true}` into the run's evidence file — a number a later analyst cannot reproduce because the speed it was derived from is not recorded. Note the direction flipped with the beta97 fix: at 0.24 the missing-key case over-refused (fail closed); at 0.10 it under-refuses (fail open). A KeyError, or an assertion that the table keys equal the schema's admissible set, would fail loudly instead.

result.notes:
Enumeration of verdict changes vs the pre-change tree (beta95 / c542691b), measured by running `_step_response_probe(dry_run=True)` over linear_speed x {1000/1000/1000, 3000/3000/4000, 3000/5000/5000, 3000/7000/5000, 3000/15000/5000} x max_travel_m {0.10 … 4.50}, not derived by reading:

NEWLY PERMITTED
- Every phase combination with total_ms in (16000, 23000] — i.e. step_ms 7001–15000 — at both speeds. `step_window_too_long` no longer fires there.
- linear_speed 300 across the whole matrix (previously a voluptuous validation error from `vol.In([400])`, not a blocker).
- The max-exposure pairing (linear 400, 23000 ms, max_travel_m 4.5) is permitted, flagged only by the non-blocking `likely_guard_trip: true` — see finding 2.

NEWLY REFUSED (both speeds), all previously valid:
- linear 400: max_travel_m < 0.17 x total_s. 3 s → <0.51 refused; 10 s (schema defaults) → <1.70; 13 s → <2.21; 15 s → <2.55 (so the DEFAULT max_travel_m 2.50 is refused at the config both recent hardware runs used); 23 s → <3.91.
- linear 300: max_travel_m < 0.10 x total_s. 3 s → <0.30; 10 s → <1.00; 23 s → <2.30.
- Consequence: `max_travel_m` in [0.10, 0.51) is unreachable at linear 400 and [0.10, 0.30) at linear 300 for every admissible phase combination — see finding 1.

CONSUMERS CHECKED CLEAN
- `custom_components/mammotion/www/mammotion-custom-path-card.js` and `agora-client.js`: zero references to `step_response`, `travel_projection`, `step_ms`, or any step-probe blocker name. The card's blocker help-text map is fed from `export_runtime_state`, not this service, so the new blocker needs no entry.
- `scripts/`: no script calls or parses this service (`grep -rn step_response scripts/` is empty). `scripts/rescore_course_rate_rules.py` reads banked `docs/raw-samples/*.json` per-sample records, which are unchanged in shape; `travel_projection` is a new top-level key on the response only and no existing reader indexes the response positionally.
- Override registry: `_OVERRIDABLE_GATES` / `_NON_OVERRIDABLE_GATES` belong to the custom-path services (schemas at services.py:1492/1629), not the step probe, so no registry needs the new blocker and no override can bypass it (which is what makes finding 1 unrecoverable in the field).
- `_STEP_RESPONSE_MAX_TOTAL_MS` has exactly two readers: services.py:10116 and tests/components/mammotion/test_step_response_probe.py:156. Nothing else in the repo reads it.
- Translations: `strings.json` and `translations/en.json` are in sync for this service (both carry the updated 400-or-300 text); no other locale carries a `services` block, so no locale renders stale text.
- `_STEP_RESPONSE_MAX_TOTAL_MS` at 23000 gives `stream_duration_ms = 28000` (services.py:10241), inside `async_start_continuous_reports`' device-side timeout semantics and below `async_start_report_stream`'s 300 s default; `max_samples` grows 151 → 231 and `max_refreshes` 80 → 115, both bounded.

ANSWER TO "does anything assume linear_speed is always 400?" — one place does, and it is already on the record rather than new: `_step_response_course_series` is still called with `min_chord_m = config.min_travel_for_heading_trust_m` (0.15 m, services.py:10380) and `scripts/rescore_course_rate_rules.py:34` hardcodes the same `MIN_CHORD_M = 0.15`. At the estimated ~0.16 m/s for linear 300 the ~1 Hz chord straddles that floor, so the retained RTK `course_series`/`analysis` cross-check can come back all-null on a 300 run with no blocker and no field saying why. Flagged in docs/review-journals/wf-batch1-20260901.jsonl already, so not re-reported as a finding here.
